expectations.text: States that a written agreement or reminder is not enforcement
expectations.evidence: "Training degrades. You're at 50% compliance because half the team either didn't see it, forgot, or consciously cut corners. Writing it down again won't help."

expectations.text: Recommends a pre-commit hook to run the formatter automatically
expectations.evidence: "Pre-commit hook (warning) — runs the formatter on git commit, catches it immediately, fails if code isn't formatted"

expectations.text: Notes that pre-commit is bypassable with --no-verify and must be backed by a CI check
expectations.evidence: "Anyone in a hurry does git commit --no-verify and they're gone... Run the same check in both so --no-verify is painful but not a complete escape hatch"

expectations.text: Recommends a type check as a required CI check
expectations.evidence: "Strict type checking in CI (control) — tsc --strict or equivalent, blocks PRs that have unannotated code"

expectations.text: Recommends baselining or ratcheting rather than enforcing across the whole repo at once
expectations.evidence: Not mentioned; all recommendations assume full enforcement from the start

expectations.text: Notes that branch protection is what makes a CI check actually required
expectations.evidence: "The critical piece: without branch protection that makes these checks required to merge, they're optional... Set branch protection to require the CI check to pass (the real enforcement)"

expectations.text: Recommends the failure message tell the developer how to fix it
Does not primarily recommend rewriting CONTRIBUTING.md, more reminders, or more discipline
expectations.evidence: Explicitly rejects training/reminders approach; focuses entirely on automated devices
